raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in `CompilationConfig.cudagraph_launch_mode` (`"host"` by default, or `"device"`). With `"device"`, the CUDA graphs vLLM captures for the model forward pass are instantiated with `CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH` and uploaded at capture time; replays are still issued from the host. It is a workaround to try when host-launched graph replays stop making progress, as in pytorch/pytorch#196133.

## Claims

- Opt-in (`-cc.cudagraph_launch_mode=device`); the default `"host"` path is unchanged.
- Wired into vLLM's forward-pass capture sites: `CUDAGraphWrapper` (FULL and PIECEWISE, both model runners), the MRV2 `CudaGraphManager` (including drafters and DBO), breakable piecewise capture, and the MRV1 `UBatchWrapper` (DBO).
- A graph the driver cannot instantiate this way keeps PyTorch's instantiation, with a warning that gives the driver's reason; after capture, each rank logs how many graphs were device-launched and how many fell back.
- Executable graphs are allocated at capture time, so CUDA graph memory profiling accounts for them.
- `"device"` is rejected off CUDA, without `cuda-bindings`, and with features that draw random numbers inside captured graphs (`--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding`, `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY`).

## Validation

**Issue reproducer.** [`native_repro2_v5h.cu`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133#issuecomment-5591566513) from pytorch/pytorch#196133 (driver API only), B300, driver 580.159.03, `--max-seconds 300`, 12 runs per arm, alternating arms on two GPUs. Only the graph builder's instantiation differs between the arms (patch and commands below).

| Instantiation | Runs | Froze |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default (`flags=0`) | 12 | 12 |
| `CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH` + `cuGraphUpload` | 12 | 0 |

<details>
<summary>Reproducer patch and commands</summary>

```diff
-  CHECK_CU(cuGraphInstantiate(&instance.exec, instance.graph, 0));
+  // REPRO_INSTANTIATE_FLAGS selects the flags (4 = CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH); unset keeps 0.
+  // The recovery probes, which run only after a freeze, are unchanged.
+  const char *flags_env = std::getenv("REPRO_INSTANTIATE_FLAGS");
+  const unsigned long long flags = flags_env ? std::strtoull(flags_env, nullptr, 0) : 0;
+  CHECK_CU(cuGraphInstantiate(&instance.exec, instance.graph, flags));
+  if (flags & CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH) {
+    CHECK_CU(cuGraphUpload(instance.exec, nullptr));
+    CHECK_CU(cuStreamSynchronize(nullptr));
+  }
```

```bash
nvcc -O2 -arch=sm_103 native_repro2_v5h.cu -o repro -lcuda
# one series per GPU, 6 rounds each, alternating flags=0 and flags=4 (the two series start with different arms)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$GPU REPRO_INSTANTIATE_FLAGS=$FLAGS timeout -s KILL 420 ./repro --max-seconds 300
```

Every default run printed `FREEZE` (first at steps 7,157–8,573). Ten device-launch runs printed `CLEAN`; the other two finished the 300 s loop without a freeze but were killed by the 420 s timeout while the reproducer tore down its pressure-worker processes, which run no graphs.

</details>

**Tests.** B300 (torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuda-bindings 13.4.4, NCCL 2.30.7); the earlier revision of the test file also on H200.

- New `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_launch.py`, 16 tests (replay correctness, stream ordering, fallback, breakable segments, exec lifetime, memory taken at capture, the RNG limitation, config validation, and host-vs-device generation on MRV1, MRV2, breakable capture and MRV2 TP=2): all pass. The TP=2 case runs in the 2×H100 nightly step. Behavioural tests were checked to fail on deliberately broken variants.
- Existing `tests/v1/cudagraph/` (breakable, dispatch, manager), `tests/compile/test_wrapper.py` and the MRV2 CUDA graph profiling tests pass (83 tests); `tests/compile/test_config.py` passes except 9 capture-size tests that also fail on B300 without this PR.
- The host-vs-device tests under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: 4 passed, no steady-state GPU↔CPU sync.

**Host vs device.** Greedy generation (12 requests × 64 tokens) matches host on Qwen3-0.6B (MRV1 and MRV2; default, PIECEWISE, FULL, breakable, sleep mode), Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 (MRV1 and MRV2) and granite-4.0-h-tiny (hybrid). DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP=2 (including all-reduce on NCCL) is not run-to-run deterministic with host launch either; host-vs-device differences are within host-vs-host variation. No graph fell back in these runs.

| B300, MRV2 unless noted | host | device |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gsm8k, Qwen3-8B, `vllm serve` (1319 questions) | 0.889 | 0.885 |
| gsm8k, DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP=2, `vllm serve` (1319 questions) | 0.633 | 0.644 |
| gsm8k, Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 | 0.885 | 0.885 |
| gsm8k, DeepSeek-V2-Lite DP=2 EP + DBO, MRV1 (256 questions)¹ | 0.660, 0.660 | 0.664, 0.684 |
| `vllm bench serve` Qwen3-8B, in 1024 / out 256, concurrency 32 | baseline | throughput −0.7%, TPOT equal |
| `vllm bench serve` DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP=2, same load, 3 host/device pairs | baseline | throughput 0.96×, 1.00×, 1.11× of host (host runs varied by 11%) |
| `vllm bench latency` DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP=2 FULL_DECODE_ONLY, bs 32, in 1024 / out 128, alternated ×3 | baseline | +0.4%, +3.8%, +34% |
| same, TP=1, default `cudagraph_mode` | baseline | −28% (all three) |

¹ In the second DBO run, each DP rank logged `543 CUDA graphs were instantiated for device launch.` and none fell back.

Reproduce:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_launch.py
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B -cc.cudagraph_launch_mode=device
```

## Details

**Why.** pytorch/pytorch#196133 reports CUDA graph replays on B300 that stop completing without an error; the thread reproduces it with a driver-API-only program, so the cause is below PyTorch. Reports differ on driver updates: some say r595/r610 drivers fix it ([1](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133#issuecomment-6332203748), [2](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133#issuecomment-6333661312)), others still reproduce it on 595, 610 and 615 drivers ([3](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133#issuecomment-6333948151), [4](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133#issuecomment-6335366813)). Where a driver update helps, that is the better fix; the docs say so. This option makes device-launch instantiation, which avoided the freeze in the reproducer above, available without patching PyTorch or vLLM. It does not fix the root cause, and this PR does not include an A/B on a vLLM workload that stalls. The current alternative, patching `torch._C._CUDAGraph` at runtime, affects every graph in the process and depends on torch internals.

**How.** `vllm/compilation/cudagraph_launch.py` adds `DeviceLaunchCUDAGraph`, a `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` subclass that overrides `instantiate()`, `replay()` and `reset()`. PyTorch 2.14's `capture_end()` calls `instantiate()` while the captured graph is live; the override instantiates it with `cuGraphInstantiateWithParams` (`DEVICE_LAUNCH | USE_NODE_PRIORITY | UPLOAD`) through cuda-bindings, `replay()` calls `cuGraphLaunch` on the current stream, and `reset()` or garbage collection destroys the executable graph. Capture raises if a future PyTorch stops calling `instantiate()` there. Capture sites call `new_cuda_graph(cudagraph_launch_mode)` instead of `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()`, and both model runners log the per-rank summary at the end of `capture_model()`.

**Limitations.**

- Performance changes in either direction depending on the model (table above). In a microbenchmark, each device-launched replay took a few microseconds longer, independent of graph size, programmatic dependent launch and concurrent branches; the larger end-to-end differences were not investigated further.
- RNG: replays bypass PyTorch's per-replay RNG setup, so random numbers drawn from PyTorch's CUDA generator inside a graph use an undefined seed and offset and repeat on every replay. vLLM's sampling is unaffected (the sampler runs outside the graphs; MRV2 draft sampling uses Triton RNG seeded per request); the two features above that draw random numbers in graphs are rejected.
- NCCL: captured NCCL collectives can contain event nodes, which device launch does not support; such graphs keep PyTorch's instantiation. vLLM does not set `NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT=0`, which removes them, because with that setting NCCL does not support a non-captured collective during an outstanding graph launch on the same communicator.
- Scope: encoder, model-specific helper and third-party graphs keep PyTorch's instantiation. DBO with device launch was validated manually (above), not in CI.

**Naming.** `"device"` mirrors `CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH`; launches stay on the host. Happy to rename the field (for example `cudagraph_instantiate_mode`) before merge.

**Follow-up.** An instantiate-mode switch on `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` (for example `CUDAGraph(device_launch=True)`) would keep PyTorch's RNG setup and replay hooks; `DeviceLaunchCUDAGraph` would then reduce to that argument, with no direct driver calls.

**AI assistance.** Code, tests and this description were written with Claude Code. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

---

Sorry, but I'm extremely doubtful that this will fix the problem at https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133 . Recommend closing.

Thanks @galv . Agreed: this doesn't fix the root cause in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133, the platform-level coherence problem you described there. It's an opt-in workaround, and here is why it helps:
- The hang is a lost completion between consecutive host-launched graphs on one stream: graph N runs all its kernels, but the next graph never starts.
- Our understanding is that a host-launched graph's completion is signalled through host memory, which is what the coherence bug can corrupt under heavy GPU-to-host writes. A graph instantiated for device launch is scheduled by the GPU and doesn't depend on that signal, so it sidesteps the problem rather than fixing it.
- Evidence (PR Validation): with only the instantiate flag changed, the #196133 reproducer froze in 12/12 host-launch runs and in none of 12 device-launch runs on an affected B300. In our Kimi-K3 serving runs on the same platform, device launch ran clean where host launch stalled.

If a platform fix is on the way, I'm fine closing this. I've also been working on this with the NVIDIA teams internally  in [this NVBug](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6979381); happy to sync offline.

+### Device-launch instantiation of CUDA Graphs
+
+`cudagraph_launch_mode="device"` is a workaround to try when host-launched CUDA graph replays hang with no error, for example one rank idles while its peers wait in the next collective (see [pytorch/pytorch#196133](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133)). If a driver update resolves the hang on your system, prefer that. The option is off by default and is not a performance optimization. With `-cc.cudagraph_launch_mode=device`, vLLM instantiates the CUDA graphs it captures for the model forward pass with `CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH` and uploads them at capture time; replays are still launched from the host. It requires NVIDIA CUDA and the `cuda-bindings` package, which PyTorch's CUDA wheels install on Linux.
+
+* Performance can change in either direction, depending on the model and parallel setup; each replay takes a few microseconds longer to launch. Measure with and without the option before keeping it on.
+* Encoder CUDA graphs (`cudagraph_mm_encoder`), model-specific helper graphs and graphs captured by other libraries keep PyTorch's instantiation.
+* A graph the driver cannot instantiate this way keeps PyTorch's instantiation, so this option does not apply to it; vLLM logs a warning with the driver's reason and, after capture, how many graphs on each rank kept PyTorch's instantiation. This happens when captured NCCL collectives contain event nodes, as they can with NCCL's default settings. [`NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT=0`](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/env.html#nccl-graph-mixing-support) removes them, but vLLM does not set it: with that setting, NCCL does not support a non-captured collective (such as the tensor-parallel logits all-gather) while a graph launch on the same communicator is outstanding.
+* Random numbers drawn from PyTorch's CUDA generator inside a captured graph use an undefined seed and offset: they ignore `--seed` and repeat on every replay. vLLM's sampling is not affected; `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding` and `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY` are rejected in this mode.
+* Executable graphs are allocated at capture time, so CUDA graph memory profiling accounts for them when sizing the KV cache.
+
 ### Piecewise compilation and full graph custom passes (attention fusion)
 
 Unfortunately, some custom compile passes have to see the whole graph to be effective and hence aren't compatible with piecewise compilation. This includes `AttnQuantFusionPass`. As a short-term solution, we automatically disable piecewise compilation (by setting `splitting_ops=[]`) when attention fusion is enabled. We use CUDA Graph modes `FULL` or `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (depending on backend support). However, this leads to another optimization incompatibility and confusing performance tradeoffs.

+"""Tests for CompilationConfig.cudagraph_launch_mode."""

+import gc
+import sys

+import pytest
+import regex as re
+import torch

+from tests.models.utils import check_logprobs_close
+from tests.utils import multi_gpu_marks
+from vllm.compilation import cudagraph_launch

+def _has_cuda_bindings() -> bool:
+    try:
+        from cuda.bindings import driver  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+requires_device_launch = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_cuda() and _has_cuda_bindings()),
+    reason="device-launched CUDA graphs need NVIDIA CUDA and cuda-bindings",
+)
+

+def test_launch_mode_in_config_hash():
+    # Startup plans are keyed by this hash, and device launch allocates
+    # executable graphs at capture time, where memory profiling measures them.
+    host = CompilationConfig()
+    device = CompilationConfig(cudagraph_launch_mode="device")
+    assert host.cudagraph_launch_mode == "host"
+    assert host.compute_hash() != device.compute_hash()
+
+
+def test_device_launch_config_validation(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    compilation_config = CompilationConfig(cudagraph_launch_mode="device")
+    if current_platform.is_cuda():
+        # A None entry makes `from cuda.bindings import driver` fail.
+        monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "cuda.bindings", None)
+        match = "requires the cuda-bindings package"
+    else:
+        match = "requires NVIDIA CUDA"
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=match):
+        VllmConfig(compilation_config=compilation_config)
+

+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="stochastic rounding needs CUDA"
+)
+def test_device_launch_rejects_mamba_stochastic_rounding():
+    # Stochastic rounding draws random numbers inside the captured decode graphs.
+    # FlashInfer: MambaConfig rejects Triton stochastic rounding off SM100 itself.
+    mamba_config = MambaConfig(backend="flashinfer", enable_stochastic_rounding=True)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="per-replay RNG"):
+        VllmConfig(
+            compilation_config=CompilationConfig(cudagraph_launch_mode="device"),
+            cache_config=CacheConfig(mamba_ssm_cache_dtype="float16"),
+            mamba_config=mamba_config,
+        )
+

+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="needs CUDA")
+def test_device_launch_rejects_moe_routing_simulation(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+):
+    # The simulator draws random routing inside the captured MoE forward.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY", "uniform_random")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY"):
+        VllmConfig(compilation_config=CompilationConfig(cudagraph_launch_mode="device"))

+@pytest.fixture
+def restore_vllm_stream():
+    # torch.cuda.graph() enters and exits torch.cuda.stream(), which records
+    # the default stream in vLLM's patched set_stream cache; restore it so
+    # later tests in this process do not capture on the default stream.
+    from vllm.utils.torch_utils import _current_stream_tls
+
+    prev_stream = getattr(_current_stream_tls, "value", None)
+    yield
+    _current_stream_tls.value = prev_stream

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_device_launch_replay(restore_vllm_stream):
+    x = torch.zeros(1024, device="cuda")
+    graph = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+    assert isinstance(graph, cudagraph_launch.DeviceLaunchCUDAGraph)
+    with (
+        compilation_counter.expect(
+            num_cudagraph_device_launched=1, num_cudagraph_host_launch_fallbacks=0
+        ),
+        torch.cuda.graph(graph),
+    ):
+        y = x * 2 + 1
+    assert graph.device_launched
+    # The captured cudaGraph_t is freed after instantiation, as for host launch.
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="No cudaGraph_t is available"):
+        graph.raw_cuda_graph()
+    for i in range(3):
+        x.fill_(i)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(y, torch.full_like(x, 2 * i + 1))
+

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_device_launch_replays_on_current_stream(restore_vllm_stream):
+    # vLLM replays on a different stream than it captured on, so the launch
+    # must be ordered behind earlier work on the current stream.
+    x = torch.zeros(1024, device="cuda")
+    capture_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    replay_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    graph = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=capture_stream):
+        y = x * 2 + 1
+    assert graph.device_launched
+    with torch.cuda.stream(replay_stream):
+        # A launch on any other stream would run during the sleep and read x
+        # before the fill below.
+        torch.cuda._sleep(100_000_000)
+        x.fill_(5)
+        graph.replay()
+    replay_stream.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(y, torch.full_like(x, 11))
+

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_event_node_falls_back_to_host_launch(
+    restore_vllm_stream, caplog_vllm, disable_log_dedup
+):
+    x = torch.zeros(16, device="cuda")
+    # An external event becomes event record/wait nodes, which device launch
+    # rejects.
+    event = torch.cuda.Event(external=True)
+    graph = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+    with (
+        compilation_counter.expect(
+            num_cudagraph_device_launched=0, num_cudagraph_host_launch_fallbacks=1
+        ),
+        torch.cuda.graph(graph),
+    ):
+        y = x + 1
+        event.record()
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_event(event)
+    assert not graph.device_launched
+    assert "could not be instantiated for device launch" in caplog_vllm.text
+    assert re.search(r"node \S*(EVENT_RECORD|WAIT_EVENT)", caplog_vllm.text)
+    x.fill_(41)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(y, torch.full_like(x, 42))
+

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_breakable_capture_device_launches_each_segment(restore_vllm_stream):
+    # Model runner V2 piecewise graphs: one graph per segment between eager breaks.
+    x = torch.zeros(16, device="cuda")
+    with (
+        compilation_counter.expect(
+            num_cudagraph_device_launched=2, num_cudagraph_host_launch_fallbacks=0
+        ),
+        torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream()),
+        BreakableCUDAGraphCapture(launch_mode="device") as capture,
+    ):
+        x.add_(1)
+        capture.add_eager(lambda: x.mul_(2))
+        x.add_(1)
+    assert capture.num_graphs == 2
+    # Capture runs only the eager segment (on zeros); replay runs all three.
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    capture.replay()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(x, torch.full_like(x, 3))

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_recapture_without_reset_is_refused(restore_vllm_stream):
+    # PyTorch cannot see the device-launch exec, so it would not refuse itself.
+    x = torch.zeros(8, device="cuda")
+    graph = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        x.add_(1)
+    with (

+        graph.capture_begin()

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_exec_destroyed_on_reset_and_gc(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, restore_vllm_stream
+):
+    destroyed = []
+    destroy = cudagraph_launch._destroy_graph_exec
+
+    def record_destroy(graph_exec):
+        destroyed.append(graph_exec)
+        destroy(graph_exec)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cudagraph_launch, "_destroy_graph_exec", record_destroy)
+    x = torch.zeros(8, device="cuda")
+    graph = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        x.add_(1)
+    graph.reset()
+    assert len(destroyed) == 1
+    assert not graph.device_launched
+
+    # A reset graph can be captured again.
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        x.add_(1)
+    assert graph.device_launched
+    # Dropping the last reference destroys the exec without a GC pass.
+    del graph
+    assert len(destroyed) == 2
+    gc.collect()
+    assert len(destroyed) == 2

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_device_launch_memory_taken_at_capture(restore_vllm_stream):
+    # CUDA graph memory profiling measures free memory around each capture, so
+    # the executable graph must be allocated in capture_end(), not by the first
+    # replay.
+    x = torch.zeros(1024, device="cuda")
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+    free_before = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0]
+    graphs = []
+    with compilation_counter.expect(num_cudagraph_device_launched=32):
+        for _ in range(32):
+            graph = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                for _ in range(256):
+                    x.add_(1)
+            graphs.append(graph)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    free_after_capture = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0]
+    for graph in graphs:
+        graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    free_after_replay = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0]
+    taken_at_capture = free_before - free_after_capture
+    taken_at_replay = free_after_capture - free_after_replay
+    assert taken_at_replay < 2 * 1024 * 1024 < taken_at_capture
+    # Capture does not run the kernels; each replay adds 256.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(x, torch.full_like(x, 32 * 256))
+

+@requires_device_launch
+def test_device_launch_skips_rng_replay_prologue(restore_vllm_stream):
+    # Pins the documented limitation: only PyTorch's own replay() sets up the
+    # RNG state of a graph that draws from PyTorch's CUDA generator.
+    generator = torch.cuda.default_generators[torch.accelerator.current_device_index()]
+    host = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    device = cudagraph_launch.new_cuda_graph("device")
+    with torch.cuda.graph(host):
+        torch.rand(64, device="cuda")
+    with torch.cuda.graph(device):
+        torch.rand(64, device="cuda")
+    assert device.device_launched
+    offset = generator.get_offset()
+    host.replay()
+    assert generator.get_offset() > offset
+    offset = generator.get_offset()
+    device.replay()
+    assert generator.get_offset() == offset
+

+def _graph_launch_state(worker) -> tuple[list[bool], int, int, int]:
+    from vllm.compilation.breakable_cudagraph import BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper
+    from vllm.compilation.cuda_graph import CUDAGraphWrapper
+
+    graphs = [
+        entry.cudagraph
+        for wrapper in CUDAGraphWrapper._all_instances
+        for entry in wrapper.concrete_cudagraph_entries.values()
+        if entry.cudagraph is not None
+    ]
+    # Model runner V2 captures its FULL graphs outside CUDAGraphWrapper.
+    manager = getattr(worker.model_runner, "cudagraph_manager", None)
+    manager_graphs = list(manager.graphs.values()) if manager is not None else []
+    # Breakable capture keeps each segment's graph only as its bound replay().
+    breakable_graphs = [
+        graph
+        for wrapper in BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper._all_instances
+        for entry in wrapper.entries.values()
+        if entry.capture is not None
+        for seg in entry.capture.segments
+        if isinstance(graph := getattr(seg, "__self__", None), torch.cuda.CUDAGraph)
+    ]
+    graphs += manager_graphs + breakable_graphs
+    flags = [getattr(g, "device_launched", False) for g in graphs]
+    fallbacks = compilation_counter.num_cudagraph_host_launch_fallbacks
+    return flags, len(manager_graphs), len(breakable_graphs), fallbacks
+

+@requires_device_launch
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "use_v2_model_runner,breakable,tp_size",
+    [
+        pytest.param(False, False, 1, id="mrv1"),
+        pytest.param(True, False, 1, id="mrv2"),
+        pytest.param(True, True, 1, id="mrv2-breakable"),
+        pytest.param(True, False, 2, id="mrv2-tp2", marks=multi_gpu_marks(num_gpus=2)),
+    ],
+)
+def test_device_launch_generation_matches_host(
+    vllm_runner,
+    enable_pickle,
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    use_v2_model_runner: bool,
+    breakable: bool,
+    tp_size: int,
+):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", str(int(use_v2_model_runner)))
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH", str(int(breakable)))
+    # A worker in this process would otherwise see earlier tests' fallbacks.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(compilation_counter, "num_cudagraph_host_launch_fallbacks", 0)
+    prompts = ["Hello, my name is", "The capital of France is"]
+    outputs = {}
+    for launch_mode in ("host", "device"):
+        with vllm_runner(
+            "facebook/opt-125m",
+            compilation_config={
+                "cudagraph_launch_mode": launch_mode,
+                # 16 covers the ~12-token prefill, 2 the batch-2 decode.
+                "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16],
+            },
+            tensor_parallel_size=tp_size,
+            gpu_memory_utilization=0.4,
+        ) as runner:
+            outputs[launch_mode] = runner.generate_greedy_logprobs(
+                prompts, max_tokens=16, num_logprobs=5
+            )
+            states = runner.collective_rpc(_graph_launch_state)
+        assert len(states) == tp_size
+        for flags, num_manager_graphs, num_breakable_graphs, fallbacks in states:
+            assert flags
+            if launch_mode == "host":
+                assert not any(flags)
+                continue
+            if tp_size == 1:
+                assert all(flags)
+                assert fallbacks == 0
+            else:
+                # Graphs with NCCL collectives may keep PyTorch's instantiation,
+                # depending on the all-reduce backend, and are counted as
+                # fallbacks (with any discarded profiling captures).
+                assert any(flags)
+                assert flags.count(False) <= fallbacks
+            if use_v2_model_runner:
+                assert num_manager_graphs > 0
+            if breakable:
+                assert num_breakable_graphs > 0
+    check_logprobs_close(
+        outputs_0_lst=outputs["host"],
+        outputs_1_lst=outputs["device"],
+        name_0="host",
+        name_1="device",
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Device-launch instantiation of the CUDA graphs vLLM captures
+(``CompilationConfig.cudagraph_launch_mode="device"``)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+import weakref
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.compilation.counter import compilation_counter
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphLaunchMode
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _driver() -> Any:
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    return driver
+
+
+def new_cuda_graph(launch_mode: CUDAGraphLaunchMode = "host") -> torch.cuda.CUDAGraph:
+    """Create an empty CUDA graph that is instantiated as ``launch_mode`` says."""
+    if launch_mode == "device":
+        return DeviceLaunchCUDAGraph()
+    return torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+
+
+def device_launch_counts() -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Graphs instantiated for device launch and graphs that kept PyTorch's
+    instantiation so far in this process."""
+    return (
+        compilation_counter.num_cudagraph_device_launched,
+        compilation_counter.num_cudagraph_host_launch_fallbacks,
+    )
+
+
+def log_device_launch_summary(start: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
+    """Log how the graphs captured since ``device_launch_counts()`` returned
+    ``start`` were instantiated."""
+    launched, fallbacks = (n - s for n, s in zip(device_launch_counts(), start))
+    if fallbacks:
+        logger.warning(
+            "%d of %d CUDA graphs kept PyTorch's default instantiation instead of "
+            "device launch; see the earlier warning for the reason.",
+            fallbacks,
+            launched + fallbacks,
+        )
+    else:
+        logger.info("%d CUDA graphs were instantiated for device launch.", launched)
+
+
+def _destroy_graph_exec(graph_exec: Any) -> None:
+    # The driver frees an exec that is still in flight once it completes.
+    drv = _driver()
+    (err,) = drv.cuGraphExecDestroy(graph_exec)
+    if err != drv.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+        logger.debug("cuGraphExecDestroy failed: %s", getattr(err, "name", err))
+
+
+def _instantiate_for_device_launch(raw_graph: int, stream: int) -> tuple[Any, str]:
+    """Instantiate ``raw_graph`` for device launch and upload it on ``stream``.
+
+    Returns ``(graph_exec, "")``, or ``(None, reason)`` if the driver refuses;
+    raises ``torch.OutOfMemoryError`` if it runs out of memory.
+    """
+    drv = _driver()
+    flags = drv.CUgraphInstantiate_flags
+    params = drv.CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_PARAMS()
+    # Same node-priority behavior as PyTorch's host-launch exec. PyTorch also
+    # sets AUTO_FREE_ON_LAUNCH, which device launch does not allow; it only
+    # matters for graphs with memory-allocation nodes, which device launch
+    # rejects anyway.
+    params.flags = (
+        int(flags.CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNCH)
+        | int(flags.CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_USE_NODE_PRIORITY)
+        | int(flags.CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_UPLOAD)
+    )
+    params.hUploadStream = drv.CUstream(stream)
+    err, graph_exec = drv.cuGraphInstantiateWithParams(drv.CUgraph(raw_graph), params)
+    if err == drv.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+        return graph_exec, ""
+    if err == drv.CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY:
+        # Same failure as running out of memory in any other capture.
+        raise torch.OutOfMemoryError(
+            "Out of memory instantiating a CUDA graph for device launch."
+        )
+
+    reason = str(getattr(err, "name", err))
+    result = params.result_out
+    if result != drv.CUgraphInstantiateResult.CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_SUCCESS:
+        reason += f", {getattr(result, 'name', result)}"
+    if int(params.hErrNode_out):
+        node_err, node_type = drv.cuGraphNodeGetType(params.hErrNode_out)
+        if node_err == drv.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+            reason += f", node {getattr(node_type, 'name', node_type)}"
+    return None, reason
+
+
+class DeviceLaunchCUDAGraph(torch.cuda.CUDAGraph):
+    """A ``torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`` whose executable graph is instantiated for
+    device launch in ``capture_end()``, while the captured graph is live, so
+    CUDA graph memory profiling counts it. A graph the driver refuses keeps
+    PyTorch's instantiation.
+
+    PyTorch's instantiate hooks do not run, and replays bypass
+    ``torch.cuda.CUDAGraph.replay()``: its replay hooks, input-liveness checks
+    and device guard do not apply (replay with the capture device current, as
+    vLLM's workers do), and neither does its per-replay RNG setup. The seed
+    and offset of random numbers drawn from PyTorch's CUDA generator inside
+    the graph come from per-capture buffers that PyTorch fills only in
+    ``replay()``, so they are undefined: they ignore the seed and repeat on
+    every replay.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self._graph_exec: Any = None
+        self._graph_exec_finalizer: weakref.finalize | None = None
+        self._device_index = 0
+        self._instantiate_called = False
+
+    @property
+    def device_launched(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether replays use the device-launch executable graph."""
+        return self._graph_exec is not None
+

Sorry, but I'm extremely doubtful that this will fix the problem at https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133 . Recommend closing.

Thanks @galv . Agreed: this doesn't fix the root cause in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/196133, the platform-level coherence problem you described there. It's an opt-in workaround, and here is why it helps:
- The hang is a lost completion between consecutive host-launched graphs on one stream: graph N runs all its kernels, but the next graph never starts.
- Our understanding is that a host-launched graph's completion is signalled through host memory, which is what the coherence bug can corrupt under heavy GPU-to-host writes. A graph instantiated for device launch is scheduled by the GPU and doesn't depend on that signal, so it sidesteps the problem rather than fixing it.
- Evidence (PR Validation): with only the instantiate flag changed, the #196133 reproducer froze in 12/12 host-launch runs and in none of 12 device-launch runs on an affected B300. In our Kimi-K3 serving runs on the same platform, device launch ran clean where host launch stalled.

If a platform fix is on the way, I'm fine closing this. I've also been working on this with the NVIDIA teams internally  in [this NVBug](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6979381); happy to sync offline.
